brief: BofA Securities weekly client flow report dated 08 September 2026, covering the week ended 9/4/26. It reports data and does not argue a directional market thesis. With the S&P 500 up 0.1%, BofA clients bought $7.0bn of US equities, a second straight inflow week, the biggest since mid-July and 6th largest since 2008. Single stocks took $3.9bn and equity ETFs $3.1bn. Institutional ($5.8bn) and hedge fund ($4.0bn) clients bought while private clients sold for a 6th week. Large and mid caps were bought, small caps sold. Stocks in 8 of 11 sectors saw inflows, led by Tech for a second week, and Industrials saw the largest outflows for a fifth week. The one interpretive link BofA draws is that Industrials selling follows the sector having been among the most crowded and expensive, with positioning starting to come off highs. Growth ETFs took inflows for the first time in 5 weeks, though Tech ETFs saw the largest sector ETF outflows against Tech's biggest single stock inflows. Corporate buybacks accelerated for a second week led by Financials, but are down 32% year over year and sit at 0.18% of S&P 500 market cap versus a 0.42% February peak.
